description: Five sourced CC0 documentary photos of human astronomical instruments, navigation, mechanical printing, a Nigerian market, and museum sculpture. Captions avoid inferring undocumented dates or identities.

images.title: Astrolabe from Lahore, 1666
images.summary: A richly engraved brass astrolabe made by Jamal al-Din ibn Muqim in Lahore in 1666, now in the Science Museum in London. This instrument exemplifies historic astronomical observation and mathematical craftsmanship.
images.alt: Intricate round golden-brass astrolabe with ring, engraved circles and patterned cutouts, photographed in a museum display case.
images.caption: The astrolabe embodies mathematical and astronomical practices. Its markings and components require additional explanations for a reader unfamiliar with historical instrument design.
images.credit: Daderot / Science Museum London (artifact by Jamal al-Din ibn Muqim)
images.rights: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, verified on the individual Wikimedia Commons file page; uploader credit and original link retained as provenance.
images.processing: Resized to a maximum 1800-pixel edge and re-encoded at JPEG quality 87 for the development archive; no synthetic elements added. Original source is linked.

images.title: Sailboat on the Adriatic Sea
images.summary: A modern sailing vessel appears against sunlit open water in the Adriatic Sea. Sailing demonstrates one means by which humans traverse bodies of water using wind and maritime navigation.
images.alt: A dark sailboat silhouette on sparkling silver sea beneath an overcast sky.
images.caption: A modern example of wind-powered ocean travel. It does not represent the diversity of vessels or seafaring traditions across history.

images.title: Historic printing press at the Chinese Writing Museum
images.summary: A printing press displayed in the Chinese Writing Museum in Anyang, China. Mechanical reproduction of text enabled books and other written materials to be copied repeatedly.
images.alt: Large dark metal printing machine displayed in museum, with Chinese character panels behind it.
images.caption: A historical printing machine exhibited in Anyang; this is an example of text reproduction, rather than a claim that printing originated with this specific machine.

images.title: Street market in Onitsha, Nigeria
images.summary: A street market in Onitsha, Anambra State, Nigeria, photographed in 2026. Stalls, customers and fish sellers illustrate everyday local trade and exchange.
images.alt: Several round basins filled with fresh fish and people beside them at a daytime street market in Onitsha.
images.caption: Trading and food distribution at a specific urban market in southeastern Nigeria. The image should be understood as one local scene, not as a proxy for all African marketplaces.

images.title: Decorative stone vase in a museum
images.summary: A sculpted ornamental vase on display in the Vatican Museums shows intentional shaping and surface patterning of stone into a decorative object.
images.alt: Large pale gray and cream marble-like urn with curved handles and organic banded patterns on a stone pedestal.
images.caption: A photographed sculptural object in the Vatican Museums; its exact maker, historical period and stone composition have not been independently established.
